name: Weit Pot
current_role: Major shareholder and former co-CEO of IMC (trading firm); listed as co-CEO of IMC Asset Management BV
profile: Wiet (Wilhelmus) Pot, born 1957 in Eindhoven, is a Dutch financier. After Chase Manhattan and 13+ years at Goldman Sachs (partner 1994), he joined Amsterdam market-maker IMC's leadership in 2007-08, serving as co-CEO alongside founder Rob Defares until leaving the board in 2017. His wealth stems mainly from a large stake in IMC.
interesting_fact: He rose at Goldman Sachs from joining in 1986 to deputy head of European equities, partner in 1994 and co-COO of the global equities division; Goldman's 1999 IPO reportedly netted him about $110m.
deep_cut_fact: A law graduate (Leiden, 1981) with an INSEAD MBA, he said he skipped becoming a notary because it would mean spending the rest of his life 'playing bridge with the mayor and the priest'. He is behind the 'Huis van Leyden' cultural restoration project at Pieterskerkhof/Rapenburg in Leiden.
notes: Name usually spelled 'Wiet Pot' (input has 'Weit'). Not an IMC founder (founders: Defares & Schelvis). Low public profile since 2017; IMC general Amsterdam email is the only published route. Runs the Wiet Pot Family Foundation (no published contact found).

name: Ye Delin
current_role: Chairman and President, New Pearl Group (新明珠集团), Foshan
profile: Ye Delin (叶德林, b. 1956, Foshan) built Guangdong's New Pearl Group into one of China's largest ceramic-tile makers. He ran the Mingzhu No.1 and No.2 factories from 1993, bought them out in 1998 and has chaired the group since. He and his wife Li Yao control ~88% of the company, which filed for a Shenzhen main-board IPO.
interesting_fact: He is a member of the executive committee of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce and vice-president of the China Building Materials Federation, and formerly chaired the Foshan Federation of Industry and Commerce for two terms.
deep_cut_fact: Before tiles, he spent 15 years (1975-1990) at the Nanzhuang hydropower station office, rising from worker to its director; he started work in 1974 as a laborer on the Nanzhuang commune construction team.
notes: IR email is from the 2023 IPO prospectus draft (board office handles disclosure/IR). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Philip Hager
current_role: Family shareholder of Hager SE (Blieskastel, Germany) per Forbes; current board role not confirmed
profile: Forbes lists 'Philip & family Hager' as major shareholders of Hager SE, the family-owned German maker of electrical installation, energy-distribution and building-automation products (brands Hager, Berker, E3/DC; ~13,000 staff). The firm was founded in 1955 by Peter Hager and sons Oswald and Hermann.
interesting_fact: Hager Group owns E3/DC, a maker of home battery-storage and energy-management systems, linking the family firm to the energy-transition theme.
notes: Could not confirm which family member 'Philip/Philipp Hager' is: a Philip Hager appears on a 2016 Hager annual-report supervisory-board page, while recent reports name Peter Hager (son of co-founder Hermann) as shareholder/board member. Possible mix-up. Very private; route via Hager Group corporate communications.

name: Peter De Haan
current_role: Private investor and philanthropist; founder/director of Opus Trust companies and director of Bancroft Wines (per MarketScreener)
profile: Peter De Haan co-ran Folkestone-based Saga, the over-50s holidays and insurance group founded by his father Sidney, alongside brother Sir Roger for about two decades until its 2004 sale (~£1.35bn). He set up the Peter De Haan Charitable Trust in 1999 and has since focused on philanthropy and private businesses including Opus Trust and Bancroft Wines.
interesting_fact: The De Haan brothers have poured large sums into regenerating their home town of Folkestone, including its Creative Quarter, harbour and Seven Hills sports ground.
deep_cut_fact: An arts philanthropist, he launched IdeasTap in December 2008, a funding and opportunities network for young creatives whose founding partners included Old Vic New Voices, the National Youth Theatre and Polka Theatre.
notes: Low-profile; no published personal or office contact found. Peter De Haan Charitable Trust (no. 1077005) was removed from the Charity Commission register in Dec 2024; a Swiss 'Fondation Peter De Haan' (Lausanne) may be his current vehicle (unconfirmed). Avoid referencing IdeasTap's 2015 closure.

name: George Steinbrenner III
profile: Principal owner of the New York Yankees from 1973; died of a heart attack in Tampa, Florida on 13 July 2010, aged 80.
interesting_fact: He died on the day of MLB's 81st All-Star Game.
notes: Deceased (13 Jul 2010). Yankees now controlled by his son Hal Steinbrenner (managing general partner) and family.

name: Jason Gardner
current_role: Founder and board director, Marqeta (NASDAQ: MQ); director, Pagaya Technologies
profile: New Jersey-born Jason Gardner co-founded rent-payments startup PropertyBridge (sold to MoneyGram in 2007), then founded Marqeta in 2010, building a card-issuing API used by DoorDash, Square and others; it IPO'd in 2021. He handed the CEO role to Simon Khalaf in 2023 and stepped down as executive chairman in June 2024, remaining a director with roughly 40% voting power.
interesting_fact: As a teen he worked at a thrift store and sold T-shirts on trains to Grateful Dead concerts; in his 20s he worked as an assistant to Senator John McCain.
deep_cut_fact: His first company, Vertical Think, was an early Elance/Upwork-style marketplace matching web developers with small projects, which he called 'more a lifestyle business'. Marqeta's original idea was a debit card that could hold many merchant coupons such as Groupon deals.
notes: No longer an executive at Marqeta, so company press may route slowly; he has done many podcast interviews (a16z, Founders Network, Stifel) and is approachable on founder topics.

name: An Xu
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Suzhou SLAC Precision Equipment Co. (斯莱克, SZSE: 300382)
profile: An Xu (安旭; English name Shu An, b. 1963, US citizen) founded Suzhou SLAC Precision Equipment in 2004 and has led it since; it listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2014. SLAC makes high-speed beverage can and can-end production lines and inspection systems sold to 20+ countries, and has diversified into battery components and automotive parts.
interesting_fact: SLAC describes itself as Asia's company consistently focused on building complete can and can-end lines; it has extended its metal-forming know-how into battery parts and holds the chair of a battery-systems firm, Ningde Juneng.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding SLAC he was an R&D engineer, project engineer and mechanical engineering manager at Stolle Machinery, a US can-making equipment maker (then an Alcoa subsidiary). He holds master's degrees from Tsinghua (precision instruments) and the University of Cincinnati.
notes: Hurun 'SLAC' = Suzhou SLAC Precision Equipment. Also on China Packaging Federation's metal-container committee. IR email is the listed company's securities-affairs mailbox (from exchange filings data).

name: Rafal Brzoska
current_role: Founder and CEO, InPost Group (parcel lockers); leads Poland's business-led deregulation initiative 'SprawdzaMY'
profile: Rafał Brzoska (b. 1977, Racibórz) founded leaflet distributor Integer in 1999 as a student, then InPost in 2006, building Europe's largest automated parcel-locker network; InPost listed in Amsterdam in 2021. In Feb 2026 InPost agreed a ~€7.8bn take-private by a consortium of Advent, FedEx, his vehicle A&R and PPF, with Brzoska staying CEO. He also champions deregulation in Poland.
interesting_fact: At Prime Minister Tusk's invitation he has led a private-sector deregulation drive; by May 2026 he said nearly 200 regulatory changes had been implemented from 500 proposals drafted in the first 100 days.
deep_cut_fact: Integer started in his third year at the Kraków University of Economics with 20,000 złoty as a website-design business; it lost money for months before pivoting to leaflet distribution. In 2023 he received the Knight's Cross of the Order of Polonia Restituta.
notes: Highly public, media-friendly CEO; active on LinkedIn/X (accounts not verified here). InPost take-private was pending regulatory approvals as of Aug 2026; IR mailbox may change after delisting. Logistics/energy angle: lockers are a low-emission last-mile model.

name: Subba Rao Jasti
current_role: Family patriarch and shareholder, Suven Life Sciences (Hyderabad); no executive role
profile: Subba Rao Jasti (born c. 1926-27) is the patriarch of the Jasti family of Hyderabad and an early investor in Suven, founded by his son Venkateswarlu Jasti in 1989 and listed in 1995. Suven was demerged in 2020; in 2021 the family sold most of its Suven Pharmaceuticals stake to Advent International, and it retains Suven Life Sciences, a neuroscience drug developer.
interesting_fact: Suven Life Sciences, the family's remaining listed company, runs a CNS drug pipeline including masupirdine (SUVN-502) for neuropsychiatric symptoms in Alzheimer's disease.
notes: Nearly 100 years old; no death report found but alive status not confirmed. Not a practical podcast guest; family business is run by son Venkateswarlu Jasti (Suven Life Sciences).
